problem: Neural Signed Distance Functions fail to reconstruct thin structures and open boundaries because they enforce strict inside-outside constraints, while Unsigned Distance Fields suffer from gradient singularities at the zero-level set.
approach: Metric-Phase Fields decouple metric proximity from topological phase by learning an unsigned metric field and a smooth phase field with a gated-metric formulation, enabling stable gradients and adaptive phase transition control.
contribution: MPFs preserve thin and layered structures more faithfully than SDF-based methods while enabling more robust training and reliable surface extraction than UDF-based approaches.

problem: Understanding the expressive power and approximation capabilities of Transformer architectures on bounded continuous function classes remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Establish precise approximation error upper and lower bounds for Hölder class functions using standard Transformers with Softmax, ReLU, and residual connections, measuring the number of blocks needed to achieve epsilon accuracy.
contribution: Prove that O(ε^(-d₀/α)) blocks suffice for approximation and Ω(ε^(-d₀/(4α))) blocks are necessary for Hölder functions, with corresponding excess risk rates for regression tasks.

problem: Despite widespread deployment of LLM-based agents in production across industries, we lack systematic understanding of what technical approaches make these deployments successful.
approach: Conduct 20 in-depth case studies with agent developers and survey 86 practitioners across 26 domains to understand why organizations build agents, how they build them, how they evaluate, and what challenges they face.
contribution: Document that 68% of production agents execute at most 10 steps, 70% rely on prompting instead of weight tuning, 74% use primarily human evaluation, and reliability remains the top development challenge.

problem: Causal discovery in location-scale noise models relies on symmetric noise assumptions, but real-world domains often exhibit skewed noise distributions, degrading method performance.
approach: SkewD uses likelihood-based estimation with heuristic search and expectation conditional maximization, extending the normal distribution framework to skew-normal settings for handling asymmetric noise.
contribution: Enable reliable causal inference in location-scale noise models under both symmetric and skewed noise, extending beyond bivariate to multivariate cause-effect inference.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for long-video understanding using uniform sampling and single-turn inference cannot effectively identify sparse critical evidence amid extensive redundancy.
approach: Video-o3 enables iterative discovery through Task-Decoupled Attention Masking to mitigate reasoning-tool heterogeneity and Verifiable Trajectory-Guided Rewards to control context growth, backed by Seeker-173K dataset of 173K tool-interaction trajectories.
contribution: Achieve 72.1% accuracy on MLVU and 46.5% on Video-Holmes, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art multi-hop reasoning methods.

problem: Predicting multiple interacting systems requires coordinated forecasts, but existing approaches predict one system at a time, missing efficiency and scalability opportunities.
approach: Equilibrium State Estimation forecasts all systems in a single pass by first estimating equilibrium state across systems, then generating holistic predictions based on deviation from equilibrium.
contribution: Achieve linear-time complexity and 10-70x speedup over state-of-the-art while maintaining accuracy on currency exchange and COVID-19 modeling tasks.

problem: Speech LLMs for emotion recognition produce ungrounded, text-biased judgments without verifiable acoustic evidence, while SSL encoders remain opaque despite strong representations.
approach: ADEPT transforms an SLLM into an agent maintaining an evolving candidate set and adaptively invoking semantic and acoustic probing tools, integrating GRPO with Evidence Trust Gate to couple tool usage with prediction quality.
contribution: Improve primary emotion accuracy while substantially improving minor emotion characterization with explanations grounded in auditable acoustic evidence.

problem: Weak-to-strong generalization for LLM training is hindered by noise and biases in weak-model outputs, limiting its applicability and robustness.
approach: Contrastive Weak-to-Strong Generalization leverages implicit rewards structurally equivalent to Contrastive Decoding, using contrastive decoding between pre- and post-alignment weak models to generate higher-quality samples.
contribution: Demonstrate consistent improvements across model families in capability transfer, denoising, and robustness compared to traditional weak-to-strong methods.

problem: Speculative decoding suffers from strictly sequential execution of drafting and verification stages, limiting inference throughput and latency improvements.
approach: MineDraft overlaps drafting for one batch with verification for another using a batch-parallel design, hiding drafting latency through careful request batching.
contribution: Achieve up to 75% throughput improvement and up to 39% latency reduction over standard speculative decoding with vLLM integration.

problem: Token mixing layers in language models face efficiency-expressivity trade-offs between decoding speed, memory requirements, and context length during causal generation.
approach: Unified framework separates direct input-output influence from recurrent information propagation, allowing states to depend on multiple past states and providing structured recurrence patterns with theoretical guarantees.
contribution: Design new recurrence patterns that provably achieve desired complexity while providing theoretical insights on expressivity tradeoffs.

problem: Open-vocabulary navigation requires agents to handle significant perception uncertainty from semantic ambiguity and model errors, but existing deterministic approaches fail to exploit global optimization opportunities.
approach: Probabilistic Scene Graph Navigation constructs a 3D probabilistic scene graph with semantic categorical distributions and proposes Multiverse Decision to sample multiple likely world settings, introducing Evidential Experience Calibrator for online lifelong adaptation.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art results with 66.1% success rate on MP3D, 44.8% on HM3D, and 67.9% on HSSD benchmarks.

problem: Training deep state space models at scale remains difficult due to poor hardware parallelization in both variational autoencoders and sequential Monte Carlo approaches.
approach: Parallel Variational Monte Carlo bridges autoencoding and SMC paradigms, enabling hardware-efficient training for both discriminative and generative state space tasks.
contribution: Match or exceed state-of-the-art performance while training 10x faster than the fastest competing SMC-based approach.

problem: Recovering parametric CAD construction sequences from geometric inputs is difficult because existing methods produce hard-to-edit formats or support only simple pipelines and low-complexity datasets.
approach: CADFit formulates reconstruction as IoU-driven optimization over structured CAD programs, incrementally fitting and validating parametric operations including extrusions, revolutions, fillets, and chamfers.
contribution: Outperform state-of-the-art mesh-to-CAD methods in volumetric IoU and Chamfer Distance while substantially reducing invalid CAD program ratios, particularly for complex designs.

problem: Accurately computing state overlaps in neural-network wave functions requires increasing Monte Carlo samples with the number of states, causing computational cost to scale quadratically.
approach: Multi-State Importance Sampling leverages samples from all states to estimate pairwise overlap, introducing Excited Pfaffians architecture to represent many states within a single neural network.
contribution: Match O(N_s^4)-scaling natural excited states while training >200x faster and modeling 50% more states; first to use neural networks to find all distinct energy levels of beryllium atom.

problem: Existing embodied benchmarks focus on task-level evaluation and fail to provide actionable insights about capability bottlenecks in multimodal LLMs.
approach: BEAR divides embodied tasks into 14 atomic skills for skill-level evaluation using a hierarchical diagnostic framework, proposing BEAR-Agent augmenting MLLMs with visual and spatial tools.
contribution: Discover that perceptual capabilities are major bottlenecks and models fail from unstable spatiotemporal modeling, achieving 17.5% relative improvement on embodied tasks.

problem: Distribution Matching Distillation for video diffusion models faces a structural bottleneck where the auxiliary score network must continuously track an evolving generator, causing training instability.
approach: Score Gradient Matching Distillation optimizes the fake score directly toward the teacher using teacher stop-gradient Fisher as objective, introducing dual potentials for outer-loop correction and inner-loop tracking.
contribution: Achieve approximately 3x training speedup and substantially improve motion dynamics for 4-step distilled models while preserving temporal consistency.

problem: Reward modeling from implicit feedback for LLM alignment is hindered by lack of definitive negative samples and selection bias where responses have heterogeneous propensities to elicit feedback.
approach: ImplicitRM stratifies training samples into four latent groups using a stratification model and derives a likelihood-maximization objective theoretically unbiased under selection bias.
contribution: Learn accurate reward models from implicit feedback and improve downstream RLHF performance across diverse LLM backbones and benchmarks.

problem: Existing Muon optimizers for training large models suffer from high sample complexity and high memory requirements.
approach: LiMuon builds on momentum-based variance reduction and randomized SVD to simultaneously achieve lower memory and lower sample complexity than Muon variants.
contribution: Achieve O(ε^-3) sample complexity for non-convex stochastic optimization with lower memory, demonstrated on Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and ViT models.

problem: Auto-bidding literature ignores coordination among multiple bidders, missing opportunities for improving returns in online advertising platforms.
approach: Coordinate auto-bidders so the highest-value bidder competes with outsiders while coordinated bidders refrain, demonstrating this mechanism dominates independent bidding.
contribution: Show coordination improves both Return-on-Spend compliance and total value accrued for participating auto-bidders across broad algorithm classes.

problem: Existing MLLM-based AI-generated video detectors suffer from hallucination and unstable reasoning, leading to high false-alarm rates and non-verifiable explanations.
approach: Hermes uses instance-conditioned retrieval-augmented generation for strategy planning, constructs a verifiable Evidence Reasoning Graph to ground reasoning in concrete evidence, and employs multi-agent deliberation to audit and refine evidence.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art performance on AI-generated video detection while producing auditable, interpretable explanations for trustworthy video forensics.

problem: The sensitivity of Wasserstein metrics to pixel-wise additive noise when treating images as discrete measures on the pixel grid is not well understood.
approach: Derive finite-sample expectation bounds for Gaussian noise model, proving error in signed 2-Wasserstein distance scales with square root of noise standard deviation.
contribution: Establish theoretical basis for benefits of Wasserstein metrics over Euclidean distance in noisy settings, supported by cryo-electron microscopy case study.

problem: Sparse autoencoders are highly unstable across training runs, producing different concept dictionaries and sparse codes, limiting their interpretability and reproducibility.
approach: Identifiable SAE addresses model properties hindering stability through minimal architectural and training changes including approximate restricted isometry conditions.
contribution: Achieve lower reconstruction error and improved stability in sparse autoencoders with theoretical grounding through dictionary learning connections.

problem: Providing non-conservative uncertainty quantification for kernel regression under non-Gaussian noise in safety-critical applications remains challenging.
approach: Propose novel non-asymptotic probabilistic uniform error bounds for kernel-based regression allowing sub-Gaussian, bounded, sub-exponential, and variance-bounded noise with correlated or uncorrelated structure.
contribution: Derive tighter uncertainty bounds applicable to broader noise classes than existing Gaussian-restricted approaches, demonstrated in safe control applications.

problem: LLM-based agents excel individually but struggle with effective collaboration in realistic human partnership scenarios.
approach: CollabBench features Diverse Player Profile Simulation for varied behaviors and Collaborative Agentic Training paradigm unifying reasoning, communication, and action via rollouts, optimized with hybrid reward balancing efficiency and affective adaptation.
contribution: Achieve 19.5% higher efficiency and 24.4% improved affective performance in collaborative games through trained models.

problem: Offline reinforcement learning struggles with generalization under distribution shift, but the role of loss landscape geometry and sharpness in this setting remains underexplored.
approach: Q-SAM applies Sharpness-Aware Minimization to offline RL by weighting sharpness objectives based on Q bounds and prioritizing samples suitable for sharpness optimization.
contribution: Consistently improve generalization performance across diverse datasets and algorithms while preserving training stability in offline RL.

problem: Real-world RL is constrained by limited data availability due to safety and cost concerns, limiting the applicability of data-hungry algorithms.
approach: Episodic Memory-Guided Controllable Experience Synthesizer uses diffusion models with episodic memory-based conditions constructed from EM, prioritizing synthesis on data most helpful for RL.
contribution: Significantly improve synthetic data quality and downstream RL performance, reducing storage and time costs by up to 8000x and 25.5x respectively.

problem: Zero-shot out-of-vocabulary detection models overfit in-vocabulary classes and confidently misclassify undefined OOV objects as semantically similar IV categories.
approach: OOVDet synthesizes region-level OOV prompts by sampling from low-likelihood regions of class-conditional Gaussian distributions and uses Dirichlet-based gradient attribution to mine pseudo-OOV images.
contribution: Effectively detect predefined classes while reliably rejecting undefined ones through low-density prior constraints.

problem: Formal theorem proving has focused on Olympiad-level mathematics, leaving undergraduate domains like optimization underserved due to significant distribution shift.
approach: OptProver mitigates distribution shift through large-scale optimization-focused data curation and specialized preference learning integrating perplexity-weighted optimization with penalties for non-progressing steps.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art Pass@1 and Pass@32 on optimization benchmarks while maintaining competitive general theorem-proving performance.

problem: Video segmentation models depend on explicit appearance memory banks and fail under large viewpoint changes and long-term occlusions.
approach: G²TAM leverages spatial consistency from 3D reconstruction, using spatially aligned geometric representations as implicit memory with cross-modal spatial encoder for visual-textual prompts.
contribution: Deliver strong cross-view consistency, promptable instance tracking, video object segmentation, and spatial reconstruction through geometry-grounded approach.

problem: Large Reasoning Models exhibit robustness failures under interruptions and dynamic context changes, but these vulnerabilities are not exposed by static evaluations.
approach: Evaluate LRMs under two dynamic scenarios: interruptions testing accuracy under budget constraints, and dynamic context testing adaptation to in-flight changes.
contribution: Demonstrate performance drops up to 60% when updates occur late in reasoning, revealing failure modes including reasoning leakage, panic, and self-doubt.

problem: Deployed language models lack capability-based access control, exposing all capabilities through a single API endpoint to all users and requests.
approach: Least-privilege language models define privilege as reachable internal computation during forward pass, proposing Nested Least-Privilege Networks with rank-indexed intervention providing reversible control.
contribution: Enable policy-usable privilege-utility frontiers with selective capability suppression and minimal collateral degradation across various deployment policies.

problem: Sparse attention reduces quadratic complexity but suffers from attention gap when applied to full-attention-trained models and capability gaps when trained purely with sparse attention.
approach: SSA integrates sparse and full attention with bidirectional attention-output alignment in feature space, proving approximation error scales linearly with dropped attention mass.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art performance under both inference modes with smooth adaptation to varying sparsity budgets and superior long-context capabilities.

problem: RLHF with noisy rewards suffers from inconsistent and erroneous feedback, but the interaction with group-based policy optimization methods remains underexplored.
approach: Noise-corrected GRPO explicitly models reward corruption as Bernoulli noise, estimating flip probabilities and debiasing the learning signal for unbiased gradient estimates.
contribution: Improve math task accuracy by up to 6.7 percentage points and code task accuracy by 1.5 under realistic reward model conditions.

problem: Existing vericoding benchmarks test individual languages or tools, making performance numbers not directly comparable across programming paradigms.
approach: AlgoVeri evaluates vericoding of 77 classical algorithms in Dafny, Verus, and Lean with identical functional contracts to reveal capability gaps.
contribution: Demonstrate that frontier models achieve 40.3% in Dafny but performance collapses to 24.7% in Verus and 7.8% in Lean, revealing systems-level and proof-construction barriers.

problem: Self-evolving language models may improve through internal supervision, but the gap between self-generated supervision and oracle-supervised training under closed-loop setup is unclear.
approach: Analyze four representative self-evolution strategies in unified offline framework using Knights and Knaves logical reasoning with deterministic solutions and controlled difficulty.
contribution: Show that self-evolution consistently improves but plateaus significantly below oracle-supervised training, with multi-turn critic-revision reaching strongest performance.

problem: Byte-level language models are useful but suffer from slow byte-by-byte autoregressive generation, limiting practical deployment.
approach: Byte Latent Transformer introduces block-wise diffusion objective for parallel byte generation, with extensions including self-speculation and diffusion-verification.
contribution: Achieve estimated memory-bandwidth cost over 50% lower than standard BLT on generation tasks through multiple inference strategies.

problem: Conformal prediction and risk control frameworks are incompatible with unsupervised generative models like LLMs and image generators.
approach: Conformal Generation extends conformal risk control to generative tasks by relaxing theoretical assumptions, unifying and generalizing previous CP applications to LLMs.
contribution: Enable formal guarantees on image generators producing non-memorized images, conversational AI asking enough clarifying questions, and agent output correctness.

problem: Existing evaluation methods for multi-modal image generation assess alignment with each modal condition in isolation, contradicting simultaneous condition alignment objectives.
approach: UFO introduces Atomized Chain-of-Evaluation paradigm decomposing omni-condition alignment into fine-grained disentangled Atomic Evaluation Units across modality-relevance classes.
contribution: Achieve highest correlation with human evaluation preferences with average improvement of 15.25%, introducing UFO-Bench for holistic customization model evaluation.

problem: Tabular regression with limited training samples and high collection costs suffers from overfitting to noisy observations.
approach: Counterfactual Residual Data Augmentation exploits residual invariance by generating realistic training samples through carefully selected feature perturbations.
contribution: Reduce MLP Regressor MSE by 22.9% and XGBoost Regressor MSE by 6.4% on average, outperforming existing data generators.

problem: Antibody expression ranking is hindered by scarcity of labeled experimental data, limiting the ability to optimize expression levels.
approach: Adapt Direct Preference Optimization to protein language models using union-masked log-likelihood approximation and IMGT-based alignment to leverage weak supervision from immunization data.
contribution: Consistently outperform baselines on most metrics using large-scale weak positive supervision on 4 million unlabeled camelid-derived antibodies.
